title: fix(plugin-form): optional injected navigation seam for submitBehavior.url redirects (#4989 defect 4)
body:
Fixes #4989

Defect 4 of the card — mount-blindness — the reopened remainder. Defects 1-3 and 5 landed in #5032; this implements the mechanism the maintainer ruled on 2026-08-17 (「同意」 batch): **optional injected navigation**.

## The defect

`ObjectForm` / `WizardForm` accept a relative in-app redirect path and travelled to it with `window.location.assign`. A rooted path resolves against the ORIGIN there, so under a mounted host — the console runs at `basename="/_console"`, which the framework CLI configures for every embedded deployment — an authored `/thanks` left the application. The destination was right and the navigation was wrong, and a published renderer cannot fix that alone: only the host knows its mount.

## What landed

**The seam — `HostNavigationContext` in `@object-ui/react`.** A host offers its own router-aware navigate; a renderer uses it when present. Absent is a supported state: `useHostNavigation()` outside a provider answers `{ navigate: undefined }` and never throws.

**The consumption — `packages/plugin-form/src/submitRedirectNavigation.ts`.** One hook now owns the delayed leg of an accepted redirect for both call sites: wait the declared `delayMs`, then travel through the host's navigate if one was injected, else `window.location.assign`. Both `ObjectForm` and `WizardForm` had byte-identical inline effects; writing it once is what stops a wizard and a flat form disagreeing about one authored destination.

**The supplier — `HostNavigationBridge`, mounted in `ConsoleShell`.** Hands over React Router's `navigate`, so the deployment's basename is applied by the router that owns the console's routes and the redirect becomes an SPA transition instead of a full page load.

## Context, not prop — the reasoning the ruling asked for

Both were available; context is the only one that reaches the call sites.

- Several of these forms arrive through `ComponentRegistry` / `SchemaRenderer` (`object-form`, `view:form`), where the shell never constructs the element and so has no prop to pass. A prop-only seam would fix directly-rendered forms and silently skip schema-rendered ones — the worst split for authored metadata.
- `ObjectForm` renders `WizardForm` / `TabbedForm` / `SplitForm` / `DrawerForm` / `ModalForm` internally, so a prop would have to be threaded through five presentations to reach the two redirect sites.
- It follows an existing precedent in the same package rather than inventing a shape: `DrillNavigationContext` is already "host-provided navigation, absent when nobody wired it", supplied by this same shell. `@object-ui/react` is the canonical home for cross-package seams here (`SchemaRendererContext` is read inside plugin-form and provided by the shell today), which is also why the instance-identity problem that killed the react-router route does not apply: plugin-form declares `@object-ui/react` as a real dependency.

Both mechanisms the ruling rejected are recorded in the module docblocks so they are not re-derived as improvements: router-presence sniffing (implicit, and unavailable anyway — reading the host's context means importing `react-router`, which this package declares nowhere and two real consumers do not install), and a `react-router` peer requirement (imposes resolution on router-less consumers).

## Nothing changes for a host that wires nothing

With no provider, behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was: one `window.location.assign` of the resolved path after the declared delay. A host with no router has no basename, so origin-rooted resolution is already correct there — the seam changes what a mounted host gets and nothing else. The contract verdict is untouched either way: a destination `@objectstack/spec` refuses is refused identically with or without a seam, so an injected navigate can never launder a value the authoring door rejects (pinned).

## One judgement call worth reviewing

`ConsoleShell` is documented as belonging inside a `BrowserRouter` and every real console puts it there, but partial trees render it bare (the existing notifications test does), and `useNavigate()` throws outside a router. Mounting the bridge unconditionally turned a documented convention into a crash for no diagnostic gain — a router-less console is already broken one component lower. **The bridge therefore supplies nothing when no router is above it**, which is exactly the seam's absent state. Note this is not the rejected "router-presence sniffing": that was a renderer discovering a router implicitly and making mount-awareness magic; here the mechanism stays explicit injection by a console that means to supply it, and the check only decides whether this supplier has anything to offer. Say the word if you want the strict version and the notifications test wrapped instead.

## Tests

- `packages/plugin-form/src/submitRedirect.injectedNavigation.test.tsx` (new, 12 cases) — seam present ⇒ the host navigate receives the RESOLVED path (interpolated + escaped) and `window.location.assign` is never called; a mounted host places it inside its mount; seam absent ⇒ the old behaviour is pinned unchanged; a refused destination reaches neither path; the declared delay, the unmount cancel, and latest-wins/exactly-once across host re-renders.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/HostNavigationBridge.test.tsx` (new, 5 cases) — against a REAL router: `/thanks` under `basename="/_console"` lands at `/_console/thanks` in `window.location`, the destination route renders (client-side transition), `replace` is forwarded, and a router-less mount supplies nothing without throwing.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/ConsoleShell.hostNavigation.test.tsx` (new, 2 cases) — that the console actually mounts the bridge, wired to its own router.
- **Replaces** `submitRedirect.mountBlind.test.tsx`, exactly as that file's docblock asked ("expected to be REPLACED, not merely re-spelled, by one asserting the mount is applied"). Its measurement is not lost: origin-root resolution is now pinned as the supported no-seam state.

### Reverse verification (measured, and one prediction was wrong)

1. **Seam ablated** (the hook always calls `window.location.assign`): **5 of 12 red** in the new plugin-form file — exactly the cases asserting a host navigate received the destination. I had predicted 8; the docblock now carries the measured number and names the survivors that are *not* change detectors for this mutation (the delay and unmount cases assert nothing was called, true under both bodies). Both pre-existing component redirect files stay entirely green, since they mount no provider — which is why the new file exists rather than more cases there.
2. **Supplier ablated** (the `HostNavigationBridge` line deleted from `ConsoleShell`): **2 red**, both in the new ConsoleShell test — and 0 anywhere else. This is why that third file exists: measured before writing it, deleting that one line restored the whole mount-blind behaviour with every test in the repository still green. A seam with no supplier changes nothing, and nothing was watching the supplier.

### Commands (all at `f7aa041`, the head of this branch)

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/src/ packages/app-shell/src/console/ packages/react/src/
  → Test Files 151 passed (151) | Tests 1525 passed (1525)
pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter @object-ui/plugin-form --filter @object-ui/react --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check
  → all three Done (includes each package's tsconfig.test.json, so the new tests are type-checked)
… same filter … lint  → 0 errors in all three (warning counts equal to main's baseline)
check:phantom-deps / check:self-import / check:control-bytes / check-changeset-presence / check-changeset-no-major  → all green
```

Dependency closure built first (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`) — without it `type-check` reports TS6305 against unbuilt `dist/*.d.ts` and reads like a real failure.

## Scope

`navigateOnSuccess` is **not addressed here** — a different declared key with its own open contract question (#5034), which this landing unblocks. Its call sites are untouched. `EmbeddableForm`'s `thankYouPage.redirectUrl` is a different key again (and often deliberately external) and is untouched.

One in-place amendment outside the new files: `.changeset/plugin-form-submit-redirect-contract-4989.md` (the unreleased changeset from #5032) said defect 4 was "not fixed" and cited the test file this PR deletes. Both statements ship in the same release as this change, so its closing paragraph now records the ruling and points at the new changeset instead of contradicting it.
